items.title: 14.5.1 Impact of burning fossil fuels on the atmosphere

blocks.text: The burning of fossil fuels is the primary cause of current climate change, altering the earth's ecosystems and causing human and environmental health problems. It affects the earth system in several ways, including greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution and volatile organic compounds (Figure 14.2).

blocks.alt: Countryside scene. Pale red arrows rise from Power stations (combustion), Motor vehicles (combustion) and Livestock to SO2, NO2 and NH3, under the heading Emitted Pollutants. Red curves carry these gases over to particles/aerosols SO4 2−, NO3−, NH4+ and down to Dry Deposition on a field and pond. Blue arrows lead from the aerosols down to Dry Deposition and to a rain cloud labelled Wet Deposition over a forested hill.
